correctness.rationale: For commutative rings Q(R)=J(R), so reduction modulo J turns the defining decomposition exactly into surjectivity of torsion units onto the residue-field units; Hensel's lemma then lifts every finite-order residue unit when the residue field is locally finite. The Z_(p) boundary follows from torsion(Q^x)={±1}.

originality.rationale: Qualified to the best of our knowledge. The recent source gives commutative examples and Q(R)=J(R) but does not state the torsion-lift criterion, the Henselian/complete-local classification, or the exact Z_(p) boundary. Targeted searches found no equivalent statement; standard Henselian root lifting is treated as prior art.

value.rationale: The result gives a complete commutative criterion for a newly introduced class, classifies all Henselian and complete local cases by their residue field, and isolates torsion lifting through the sharp Z_(p) versus Z_p contrast.

disclaimer: Not independent validation, peer review, formal verification, or a guarantee of first discovery.
